::: {.callout-note}
#### These notes write the full form

In these notes,
we avoid notational shorthands in permanent writing
and write the full form of each expression,
even where a shorthand would be shorter.
A reader who supplies the missing part of a shorthand
from a different context than the writer intended
reads a different expression than the one the writer meant.
Handwritten board work is often less complete,
but it should still write out ranges and limits where it can.

We make one exception:
writing two factors side by side means multiplying them,
as in $2x$ for $2 \cd x$ and $ab$ for $a \cd b$.
We still write the multiplication sign
when the side-by-side form could be misread:

- $2 \cd 3$, not $23$, which reads as twenty-three;
- $a \cd (b + c)$ when $a$ could be a function,
  since $a(b + c)$ could mean $a$ evaluated at $b + c$.

:::
